sweep.row_level_control: the decisive measurement, on Cube.exe. Comparing `xrefs --from` bucket by bucket, 16 rows appear to LEAVE a bucket -- all of them jump rows in the three zlib functions. Every one of the 16 is still present globally: `xrefs --to` each of their targets (0x40fa3d, 0x40fa41, 0x40fa52, 0x41060f, 0x410703) returns the same source addresses on both builds, with additions and no removals (0x40fa41 goes 14 -> 28 sources). What moved is the per-function BUCKET, because `finish()` groups a row by the nearest preceding entry in the walk's own function set and that set grows as more code is decoded. No reference row is lost anywhere in the sweep.
sweep.owner_reattribution: three strings on Cube.exe change owner (0x40f46c -> 0x40f134, 0x4104b8 -> 0x40fb80 x2), and both moves are onto the containing inventory function: 0x40f46c lies inside sub_40f134's 2636-byte extent and 0x4104b8 inside sub_40fb80's 3104-byte extent. These are zlib inflate's error messages, which were attributed to an address INSIDE inflate because the real entry's descent could not get past the state->mode switch. kuna functions is byte-identical before and after (479 entries both), so the inventory is untouched -- only the walk's own speculative function set moved.
sweep.decompiled_c_unchanged: structurally: the index is read-only, commits nothing, and its only non-query consumer is decompile-all's --reachable-from selection. No emitted C can change, which make test (675/675) and make test-stages confirm.

decisions: The refuter's diagnosis is UPHELD exactly as written, including its scope correction: the defect is in kuna-analysis's listing/xrefs.rs descent, not in strings.rs or the string scan, and the fix is jump-table target enumeration. The filed hypothesis ('the reference walk may miss this switch branch') is upheld as a symptom description but understates it -- it is not this switch branch, it is every switch case body in every binary.

The table base is taken from the Data-kind references data_refs ALREADY files for the instruction, not from a new pattern match. That is what keeps the rule format-independent and what keeps an import veneer out of it: `jmp qword ptr [__imp_X]` and an ELF PLT entry encode their slot as a data-space varnode, which data_refs files as a Read, so a veneer can never be read as a one-entry table of whatever its unrelocated slot holds.

Entries are queued on the INSTRUCTION queue, not the function queue: a case body is the dispatcher's own code, and recording each as a function entry would answer `sub_<case body>` to the question the need is about.

MIN_ENTRIES is 2. A compiler does not lower a one-case switch through a table, and one plausible word after a constant is a coincidence -- this is the clause that keeps a stray in-range constant on some other computed jump from fabricating a target.

Entries are confined to the executable section CONTAINING the dispatch rather than to the executable partition as a whole, so a table cannot carry the walk into a different section's code. Image-base-relative tables (MSVC x64 RVA dwords) therefore recover nothing rather than something wrong; that is a separate feature, not a silent half-answer.
No option, no phases.toml row, no catalog counter and no tests/stages case: tooling track, and the xref index is read-only, commits nothing into the engine and cannot change emitted C.

`aif` was considered as a covered-by-option answer and rejected. Neither kuna strings nor kuna xrefs accepts --option, so it is not reachable from the probe at all; and even where the gap-walk does fire it answers with a speculative entry inside the function rather than the function -- which is precisely what this change replaces on Cube.exe.
